question: Do the Chiaki references in Asobi come from the psn-api npm package, as the developer said?

developer_claims.text: all the other references are from the psn-api library I use for obtaining the little-endian/base64 encoded ID which incidentally has named that id chiaki-id. (see link https://www.npmjs.com/package/psn-api)

source_repository.head: 1e9d9a806fcd884a4ddee8086bfe92594611da9f
source_repository.method: git grep -i 'chiaki' in the tree of every commit on every branch and tag; git log -G'chiaki' --regexp-ignore-case over all history

npm_package.method: downloaded every published tarball from registry.npmjs.org and searched all files case-insensitively for 'chiaki'

asobi_strings_he_attributed: "Chiaki ID not found. Please sign out and sign in again." (1.0.9)
result: The word 'chiaki' in any spelling (chiaki-id, chiakiId, chiakiEncodedId) has never appeared in psn-api's source history or in any of its published npm packages. The name did not come from psn-api. The base64 little-endian account-ID format he describes is the format Chiaki asks users to enter when registering a console.
npm_to_github_link: Every one of the 37 npm releases names https://github.com/achievements-app/psn-api as its repository, and the gitHead commit npm recorded for each release exists in that repository (37 of 37). Each release also has a matching git tag. The package the developer linked on #725 (https://www.npmjs.com/package/psn-api) is therefore built from the repository searched here.
